value.behaviour: jsdom tests of the card's list, states, mark-as-read, deep links, signal refresh, polling fallback and cleanup.
rules: Render with `renderInTestApp` from '@backstage/test-utils' inside `TestApiProvider`, with `mountedRoutes: { '/notifications': rootRouteRef }` ('../../routes'), and provide `[notificationsApiRef, api]` and `[toastApiRef, { post }]` in every test.
Build mocks inside each test or in `beforeEach`, and make `getNotifications` return what the backend would after the update under test, because a successful mark-as-read refetches.

Signals available means `[signalApiRef, { subscribe }]` from '@backstage/plugin-signals-react', where `subscribe` captures `onMessage` and returns `{ unsubscribe }`; publish with `act(() => onMessage(message))`. Signals unavailable means leaving `signalApiRef` out.

Do not use fake timers. `jest.spyOn(global, 'setInterval')` and `jest.spyOn(global, 'clearInterval')`, find the call whose delay is 60000, and run its callback inside `act` to stand in for the interval elapsing. Other intervals from testing-library are ignored by that filter. Restore spies in `afterEach`.
A test that needs a fetch held open uses a promise it resolves itself.

tests.name: lists the latest unread notifications and links each to the notifications page
tests.given: getNotifications resolves two notifications, one with an id holding a slash
tests.expect: getNotifications was called with { read: false, limit: 5, sort: 'created', sortOrder: 'desc' }; both titles show; each link's href is /notifications?id=<encoded id>

tests.name: shows the loading, empty and error states inside the card
tests.given: One render each, beside a sibling element: a pending fetch, an empty list, a rejected fetch
tests.expect: The `progress` element, then 'No unread notifications', then the error message; the sibling still renders after the failure

tests.name: marks an item as read and keeps it when that fails
tests.given: Two items; updateNotifications rejects once and then resolves, and the list after success no longer holds the item
tests.expect: After the failed click the item stays and toast post was called with the failure title and status 'danger'; after the next click updateNotifications was called with { ids: [id], read: true } and the item is gone

tests.name: refetches on signals that change unread items and does not poll
tests.given: Signals available; publish new_notification, notification_read, notification_unread and one unrelated action, awaiting each refetch
tests.expect: The notifications channel is subscribed; each of the three actions causes one more getNotifications and the list updates; the unrelated action causes none; setInterval was never called with 60000

tests.name: refetches every 60 seconds without overlap when the signal API is not installed
tests.given: Signals unavailable; run the 60000 ms callback once and await the refetch, then hold the next fetch open and run the callback twice more
tests.expect: One refetch per tick; while a fetch is open no second one starts; once it resolves exactly one follow-up fetch runs

tests.name: releases the subscription and timers on unmount and fetches no more
tests.given: One render with signals and one without, each unmounted
tests.expect: unsubscribe was called once; clearInterval was called with the id setInterval returned; running the captured callback after unmount leaves the getNotifications call count unchanged

value.behaviour: jsdom tests of the `?id=` deep link on the notifications page.
rules: Render `NfsNotificationsPage` from './NotificationsPage' with `renderInTestApp` from '@backstage/test-utils', inside `TestApiProvider` with `[notificationsApiRef, api]` and `[toastApiRef, { post }]`, and `routeEntries: ['/?id=<id>']`.
The mock api provides `getNotifications`, `getNotification`, `getStatus` (`{ unread, read }`) and `getTopics` (`{ topics: [] }`).
Find the highlight with `(await screen.findByText(title)).closest('[aria-current="true"]')`; the absence of any highlight with `document.querySelector('[aria-current="true"]')`.

tests.name: shows and highlights a notification the filters would hide
tests.given: ?id=hidden; getNotifications resolves five other notifications, and getNotification resolves a read notification
tests.expect: getNotification was called with 'hidden'; its title is inside the highlight; all five other titles still show

tests.name: shows a notification from the current page only once
tests.given: ?id=n-1; getNotifications and getNotification both return n-1
tests.expect: The title appears once, inside the highlight

tests.name: treats a failed lookup as nothing to highlight
tests.given: ?id=gone; getNotification rejects with an error whose message is 'lookup failed'
tests.expect: The list renders, no highlight exists, and 'lookup failed' is not shown

tests.name: does not look anything up without an id
tests.expect: The list renders, getNotification was not called, and no highlight exists

value.behaviour: jsdom tests that the plugin exports the card as a home page widget and that the widget renders with its title.
rules: Import `createExtensionTester` and `renderInTestApp` from '@backstage/frontend-test-utils', the plugin as the default export of './alpha', `HomePageWidgetBlueprint` from '@backstage/plugin-home-react/alpha', and `rootRouteRef` from './routes'.
Get the extension with `plugin.getExtension('home-page-widget:notifications/unread-notifications')` and its data with `createExtensionTester(extension).get(HomePageWidgetBlueprint.dataRefs.widget)`.
Render `data.component` with `apis: [[notificationsApiRef, { getNotifications }], [toastApiRef, { post }]]` and `mountedRoutes: { '/notifications': rootRouteRef }`.

sites.first_line: You can customize the sidebar item using its [properties](https://backstage.io/api/stable/functions/_backstage_plugin-notifications.index.NotificationsSidebarItem.html) to fit your specific needs.
sites.rule: Add a `### Unread notifications card` section: the extension `home-page-widget:notifications/unread-notifications` is offered under **Add Widget** in the new frontend system with no configuration; it lists the 5 latest unread notifications, each with a mark-as-read action and a link to the notifications page. With the signal API installed the card refreshes on notification signals and does not poll; without it the card refreshes every 60 seconds. It must state: when signals are installed but the connection is down, the card gets no live updates and does not poll. Then add a `### Linking to a notification` section: `/notifications?id=<id>` shows and highlights that notification even when the current filters or pagination would hide it; if the notification cannot be loaded, for example because it was deleted or belongs to someone else, the page renders as it does without `?id=`.

rules: The text, for adopters and naming no internal symbols: Added an **Unread notifications** home page widget for the new frontend system. It lists your latest unread notifications with a mark-as-read action and a link to each one, and updates live through signals, or every 60 seconds when signals are not installed. The notifications page now shows and highlights the notification given by `?id=<id>`, even when the current filters or pagination would hide it.

The text, for adopters and naming no internal symbols: Card extensions now render when no app context is available, using the default progress indicator instead of throwing. Apps with an app context keep using their own progress component.
